steps.prompt: Work out $99 \times 101$ in your head, without writing anything down. What trick did you use?

cards.title: Look for structure first
cards.body: AMC arithmetic is never meant to be slogged out. If a calculation looks huge, look for a common factor ($17 \times 23 + 17 \times 77 = 17 \times 100$), numbers near a round number, or a square hiding inside. A minute spent looking saves five spent multiplying, and avoids slips.

steps.text: Use $a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$ with $a = 53$ and $b = 47$.
So $53^2 - 47^2 = 6 \times 100 = 600$, with no squaring at all.

cards.title: Near a round number
cards.body: Write numbers as a round number plus or minus a little. $99 \times 101 = (100 - 1)(100 + 1) = 100^2 - 1 = 9999$. For squares, $(a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$: $49^2 = (50 - 1)^2 = 2500 - 100 + 1 = 2401$.

cards.title: Worked example: a fraction with squares

steps.text: The top is a difference of squares: $(1001 - 999)(1001 + 999)$.

cards.title: The common trap: $a^2 - b^2$ is not $(a - b)^2$
cards.body: $53^2 - 47^2 = 600$, but $(53 - 47)^2 = 36$. Likewise $(a + b)^2$ has a middle term: $(50 + 1)^2 = 2500 + 100 + 1$, not $2500 + 1$. If your shortcut gives a suspiciously tiny answer, check which identity you used.

prompts: What will make you stop and look for a shortcut before you start multiplying?
